author: Simple Container maintainers <security@simple-container.com>
tooling: Hand-authored. Reachability evidence from `govulncheck -mode=source ./...`, `go list -deps ./...` and `go mod why -m`.

vulnerability.name: GO-2022-0635
vulnerability.description: In-band key negotiation issue in AWS S3 Crypto SDK for golang. Affected symbols: github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto NewDecryptionClient, NewEncryptionClient.

statements.impact_statement: Corrected 2026-08-10 (was wrongly `fixed`). The advisory has `introduced: 0` and NO fix event in OSV: AWS never patched the v1 s3crypto client, the remediation is migrating to the V2 encryption client. `fixed` was therefore never a reachable status and was acting as an indefinite suppression. The accurate finding: aws-sdk-go v1.55.8 still appears in the module requirement graph (`go list -m all`) because a transitive dependency's go.mod names it, but ZERO of its packages are linked into any binary we ship — `go list -deps ./... | grep -c '^github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/'` returns 0 and `go mod why -m github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go` reports "main module does not need module github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go". The s3crypto package specifically is never imported; S3 access goes through aws-sdk-go-v2. Neither govulncheck -mode=source nor osv-scanner reports this advisory against the repo, so no osv-scanner.toml mirror entry is required. Closing condition: the requirement edge disappears from `go list -m all`, at which point this statement can be deleted.

vulnerability.name: GO-2022-0646
vulnerability.description: CBC padding oracle issue in AWS S3 Crypto SDK for golang. Affected symbols: github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto NewDecryptionClient, NewEncryptionClient.

statements.impact_statement: Same module, same evidence and same correction as GO-2022-0635 — see that statement. Also `introduced: 0` with no fix event, so it was likewise mis-stated as `fixed` before 2026-08-10.

vulnerability.name: GO-2026-5932
vulnerability.description: The golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package is unmaintained, unsafe by design, and has known security issues. Affected packages: golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp and its subpackages (armor, clearsign, elgamal, errors, packet, s2k).

statements.impact_statement: Re-confirmed 2026-08-10 against the current tree: golang.org/x/crypto is a direct dependency for chacha20poly1305 only (pkg/api/secrets/ciphers). No package in the build graph imports golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp or any of its subpackages — `go list -deps ./... | grep golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp` returns nothing, so the Go linker never includes that code in any produced binary. OpenPGP operations go through github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto v1.1.6, the maintained fork the advisory itself recommends. govulncheck -mode=source ./... reports 0 reachable vulnerabilities. Unfixable by bumping: the advisory has `introduced: 0` and no fix event; it is a permanent 'package is unmaintained' notice. x/crypto is kept current regardless — pinned at v0.54.0, which is the latest release.
